item.title: Weekly Update on Concerts and Testing
item.description:
Third graders performed in a concert on Wednesday evening, and fourth graders attended Ag Day at the high school to learn about the agriculture program. Students in grades 3-5 continue working on Ohio State Tests, with the final week of state testing scheduled for next week (3rd and 4th graders taking math tests, 5th graders taking science tests). Kindergarten through 3rd grade students will take spring MAP tests in the coming weeks.

item.title: Every Kid Healthy Week Activities
item.description:
Action for Healthy Kids presents Every Kid Healthy Week from April 20th-24th with daily themed activities: - Mindfulness Monday (April 20): Journaling, deep breathing, and sharing gratitude - Tasty Tuesday (April 21): Try new foods, help prepare meals, have an indoor picnic - Wellness Wednesday (April 22): Go for a walk, play outdoor games, have a dance party - Tech-Free Thursday (April 23): Device-free meals, turn off electronics for 1 hour for reading/arts/games - Family Friday (April 24): Pick a family activity and share appreciation for each family member

Families are encouraged to take pictures participating in activities and post on social media with #HealthyLikeRox.

item.title: PAX Good Behavior Game Program
item.description:
The PAX Good Behavior Game is a research-based classroom strategy that helps students make positive choices and collaborate with others. It promotes a calmer, more focused learning environment through kindness, teamwork, and respectful behavior.

The April 2026 student calendar includes daily PAX activities such as National Walking Day (April 3), World Health Day (April 6), Earth Day activities (April 22), and National Superhero Day (April 28), along with prompts for students to practice leadership, gratitude, and positive behaviors throughout the month.

item.title: Allergies or Cold: Know the Difference
item.description:
The school nurse provides a flowchart to help distinguish between allergy symptoms and cold symptoms. Key differences: Allergies typically involve clear mucus, seasonal occurrence, itchiness, and symptoms that last for extended periods. Colds usually present with green or yellow mucus, fever, body discomfort, and symptoms that come on quickly and taper off fairly rapidly. Call your doctor if symptoms last longer than two weeks, symptoms worsen or new symptoms develop, you have a sore throat or fever higher than 100 degrees for longer than three days, or you experience intense chest pain and shortness of breath.

item.title: Allergies or Cold Decision Guide
item.description:
The school nurse provides a visual flowchart to help determine whether symptoms indicate allergies or a cold. Key differences: allergies typically cause itchy eyes/nose/throat, clear mucus, and symptoms that occur seasonally or persist for extended periods; colds typically cause green/yellow mucus, body discomfort, fever, and symptoms that come on fast and taper off quickly. Call your doctor if symptoms last longer than two weeks, worsen or new symptoms develop, you have a sore throat or fever higher than 100 degrees for longer than three days, or you experience intense chest pain and shortness of breath.
